root_idea.summary: The root centers on persistent adherence, sustained effort, and continuing in a course.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development runs from striving and maintaining continuous activity to an established custom, manner, or state of affairs. The active participle describes what continually pursues a course, while Form IV causatively makes another or something persist or exert itself.

senses.definition: Sustained and regular continuance; carrying on a course persistently.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a verbal noun in the Quranic expression of maintaining an activity continuously and regularly; in 12:47 it conveys carrying on a prescribed course as usual.

senses.definition: An established custom, habitual course, or manner of conduct.
senses.usage_conditions: In كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ and related comparative constructions, it denotes the continuing course or customary behavior of the people being compared.

senses.definition: A case, state, condition, or situation.
senses.usage_conditions: The same comparative construction may refer to the situation or plight of those being compared.

senses.definition: Persistent striving, laboring, or toiling in a continuing course.
senses.usage_conditions: An explicitly attested Quranic interpretation of كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ understands the expression as referring to their sustained exertion in unbelief and their concerted opposition and mutual support against Moses. Lane’s historical citation notation is not used as a modern verse location.

senses.definition: Continuously pursuing or maintaining a course; unceasing in its movement.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic dual دَائِبَيْنِ, it describes the sun and moon as continually pursuing their respective courses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive, labor, toil, or exert oneself, becoming weary; to persist or continue in work, a journey, or another undertaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb and its ordinary verbal usage; the subject is not restricted to a particular type of person or creature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of driving vehemently; driving away, pursuing, or hunting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verbal-noun usage distinct from the meanings of custom and persistent continuance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause another or something to strive, labor, toil, or become weary; to make it persist or continue, or to put it in need of sustained effort.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative construction, including causing someone or something to pursue a journey laboriously or with energy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An affair, business, or concern; a case, state, condition, deed, or work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Broader Classical Arabic uses of the noun beyond the Quranic comparative interpretations listed under the Quranic form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Persistent, energetic, and laborious in doing a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of sustained effort or energetic persistence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Striving, laboring, toiling, or exerting oneself, with associated weariness, in work or an undertaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in the expression لَيْلَةٌ دَائِبَةٌ for a hard, fatiguing, or continuous night journey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conventional dual epithet for the night and day as the pair that continually follows its alternating course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical Classical Arabic expression; it is distinct from the Quranic dual in 14:33, which refers to the sun and moon.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The verb’s striving and continuing meanings are represented, including its Quran-attested interpretation of persistent exertion.
The specialized meaning of vehement driving or pursuit is represented.
The Form IV causative meanings are represented.
Laborious pursuit or continuation of a journey is covered by the Form IV causative entry.
The Quranic custom, case, and persistent-striving interpretations and the broader affair/state meanings are all represented.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the preceding paragraph.
The distinct adjective دَؤُوبٌ and its energetic-persistence meaning are represented.
The active participle’s continuing and striving branches are represented separately according to Quranic and broader Classical evidence.
The conventional description of a hard or continuous night journey is included in the active-participle entry.
The conventional dual expression for night and day is represented as a Classical-only usage.

cautions: The Quranic comparative phrase كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ supports more than one lexically attested interpretation: established custom or course, case or state, and persistent striving. Contextual English glosses alone do not resolve among these readings.

The Classical expression الدَّائِبَانِ for night and day is distinct from the Quranic دَائِبَيْنِ in 14:33, where the supplied Quran-focused evidence identifies the sun and moon as continually pursuing their courses.
Lane’s historical Quran citation conventions have not been converted into modern verse keys; modern examples use only the independently supplied QAC locations.
